\section[adottare]{adottare — to adopt}

\label{lesson:IT-C495-adottare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to break up, then the Italian for to remarry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: adottare}
\textbf{adottare} — \textquotedblleft{}to adopt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hanno adottato una bambina di due anni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They adopted a two-year-old girl.}
\end{quote}

Also for ideas: \emph{adottare un metodo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{adottare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{adoptāre} \textquotedblleft{}to choose, to adopt\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{ad-} and \emph{optāre} \textquotedblleft{}to choose\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adottare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adottare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{adottare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to break up, then the Italian for to remarry, then say \emph{adottare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does adottare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To adopt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'adozione]{l'adozione — adoption}

\label{lesson:IT-C495-adozione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to remarry, then the Italian for to adopt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'adozione}
\textbf{l'adozione} — \textquotedblleft{}adoption\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'adozione è durata più di un anno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The adoption took more than a year.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Figlio adottivo} — adopted son.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{adozione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{adoptiō} \textquotedblleft{}adoption\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{adoptāre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il patrigno]{il patrigno — stepfather}

\label{lesson:IT-C495-patrigno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to adopt, then the Italian for adoption.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il patrigno}
\textbf{il patrigno} — \textquotedblleft{}stepfather\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il mio patrigno è un uomo gentile.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My stepfather is a kind man.}
\end{quote}

Built on Latin \emph{pater} \textquotedblleft{}father\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{patrigno} is usually traced to Late Latin \emph{patrignus}, built on \emph{pater} \textquotedblleft{}father\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il patrigno}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to adopt, then the Italian for adoption, then say \emph{il patrigno} again

\section[la matrigna]{la matrigna — stepmother}

\label{lesson:IT-C495-matrigna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for adoption, then the Italian for stepfather.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la matrigna}
\textbf{la matrigna} — \textquotedblleft{}stepmother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Con la mia matrigna parlo di tutto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I talk about everything with my stepmother.}
\end{quote}

Fairy tales gave the word a bad name; in real life many say \emph{la compagna di mio padre}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{matrigna} is usually traced to Late Latin \emph{mātrīnia}, built on \emph{māter} \textquotedblleft{}mother\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short); EtymDB links it to \emph{madre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la matrigna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la matrigna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la matrigna}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for adoption, then the Italian for stepfather, then say \emph{la matrigna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[il fratellastro]{il fratellastro — half-brother, stepbrother}

\label{lesson:IT-C495-fratellastro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for stepfather, then the Italian for stepmother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il fratellastro}
\textbf{il fratellastro} — \textquotedblleft{}half-brother, stepbrother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho un fratellastro più piccolo di dieci anni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have a half-brother ten years younger.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La sorellastra} — half-sister. In other words \emph{-astro} can sound negative; here it is neutral.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fratellastro} is built on \emph{fratello} \textquotedblleft{}brother\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Late Latin \emph{frātellus}, a little form of \emph{frāter} \textquotedblleft{}brother\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with the ending \emph{-astro}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il fratellastro}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il fratellastro}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il fratellastro}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for stepfather, then the Italian for stepmother, then say \emph{il fratellastro} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
